rina: FYI VertexEdge reported a ~$4.6k discrepancy after marketplace rollup. they say some minute deltas were applied twice across hour boundaries due to connector clock skew and our merge strategy. tagging partners/ops.

paul: can you attach a tiny sample? clock skew + late arrival often looks like event_time != ingestion_time and our window assignment uses ingestion_time if event_time missing.

cheng: sample attached. partner events include event_time but some devices had clocks ~5-10 minutes fast. when those minute deltas arrive late, our re-bucketing puts them in neighboring hour and checkpoints cause both windows to reflect usage.

mona: so root cause = inconsistent use of event_time vs ingestion_time + checkpointing that allows overlapping application.

rina: short-term guard: treat any incoming delta with event_time present as authoritative for window assignment; reject/flag ones where event_time differs from ingestion_time by >5 minutes and mark as "clock-drift" for manual review.

paul: long-term fix: introduce monotonic watermarks per partner source derived from max(event_time) - allowed_lag and use that to close windows. also add a reconciliation step that drops duplicates where same (device_id, event_time, metric) applied to >1 window.

recon-bot: created ticket PRJ-9999 "vertexedge-clock-drift-watermark" assigned to @cheng. (https://redwood.atlassian.com/PRJ-9999) :robot_face:

cheng: playbook sketch:
- run a lightweight dedupe: find (device_id, event_time, sum) duplicated across adjacent hours -> compute ledger delta CSV
- partners sign-off -> apply compensating adjustments via ledger-service compensations API
- implement watermark logic and alert when >0.15% of events flagged as clock-drift for partner

mona: owners/ETA:
- cheng: dry-run dedupe + CSV for partner (ETA 1 day)
- paul: add ingestion guardrail & alert rule (ETA 1 day)
- rina: draft partner comms and legal route (ETA 1 day)

rina: scheduling a sync with VertexEdge tomorrow 10:30am PT to walk through proposed watermark approach. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
